claims.text: Selective chromium oxidation governs the formation and persistence of a protective oxide layer in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
Minor Si additions substantially enhance selective chromium oxidation.
Minor Al additions substantially enhance selective chromium oxidation.
Si promotes formation of a mixed Cr2O3-SiO2 surface scale.
Al promotes formation of a mixed Cr2O3-Al2O3 surface scale.
The proposed mixed oxide scale is dense and coherent with the underlying alloy substrate.
The mixed oxide scale enhances adhesion and minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch.
The mixed oxide scale is better able to accommodate thermal and oxide-growth stresses.
Minor Si additions reduce the activation energy for selective chromium oxidation.
Minor Al additions reduce the activation energy for selective chromium oxidation.
Mn does not provide the oxide-structure benefits attributed to Si or Al.
Mn-containing alloys form non-coherent, unstable oxides prone to cracking and spallation.
Si-containing alloys will form more stable, adherent, and coherent oxide scales than the Mn-containing baseline.
Al-containing alloys will form more stable, adherent, and coherent oxide scales than the Mn-containing baseline.
Si- and Al-containing alloys will have improved resistance to thermally induced spallation relative to Mn-containing alloys.
Mn-containing alloys are expected to form thinner oxide scales than Si- or Al-containing alloys.
The hypothesis is scoped to CrFeCoNiX alloys initially in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state and exposed above 900 °C in a controlled oxidative or corrosive environment.
Additional mechanical stresses and deviations in alloy composition are outside the proposed scope.
